findings.claim: The observed window is the native endpoint-coordinate score clock [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score nodes; curve support is only [0.0,0.49], so no evidence exists beyond the observed support and extrapolation is disallowed.

Continuous contrast functions over the observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with first_rate_z +9.27 and last_rate_z -10.00, and landmark_00_local_dz shows 10 sign changes; a constant rule is therefore not supported and a time-conditioned rule is indicated, but no polynomial fit is accepted (polynomial_accepted=false) and relative node RMSE is large (0.29-0.78), so these are descriptive contrast curves, not absolute reward targets.

Joint selection-innovation diagnostics show a coherent positive association of innovation_native_alignment (mean 0.092, q=2.2e-9, positive_batch_fraction 1.0) and high teacher_contrast_coherence (mean 0.812), while observed_child_score_gain is negative (mean -0.036, q=1.8e-7, positive_batch_fraction 0.0); immediate selection evidence and later observed child credit disagree in sign, so direction priorities should not be set from point estimates alone.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control; recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal-score, so no decoded terminal affinity labels are available and last-record or child-score credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: No reduction in sign-change mismatch or node RMSE versus the constant rule on held-out observed nodes.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dz contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast at observed selection nodes, using the validated absolute contrast change to modulate regional attention, will track the sign-changing landmark_00_soft_mass and local_dz contrasts better than a constant contrast rule.

hypotheses.falsifier: Adjusted ranking is identical to the point-estimate ranking.
hypotheses.observable: rank order of coordinate hypotheses under q-values and positive_batch_fraction versus raw means
hypotheses.scope: within-selector joint diagnostics, batch as independent unit
hypotheses.statement: Prioritizing coordinate hypotheses by multiplicity-adjusted support and coverage rather than point estimates will reorder candidates, because the negative observed_child_score_gain conflicts with the positive innovation_native_alignment association.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record and child-score credit are not final affinity benefit and the unavailable comparison is reported rather than substituted.
Continuous contrast fits are not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false) and extrapolation is disallowed, so only observed-node interpolation is supported.
Joint diagnostics are descriptive within-selector associations; batch is the independent unit and no causal selection effect or atom velocity is claimed.
No current study outcome data are available to this role, so no reward recipe is asserted as validated.
